findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, against the 1.63.0 report's item 'memory-search-hybrid-retrieval'
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The 1.63.0 run recorded that the semantic query 'an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light inside a stargazing room' is one 'that keyword match cannot carry', and backed it with two observations: a keyword-only control (vectorWeight 0) returning 'results: []', and the bank agreeing that the keyword leg has nothing - 'SELECT count(*) FROM entries_fts WHERE entries_fts MATCH ...' -> 0.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The premise does not hold, and did not hold in 1.63.0 either - the prior run's two observations were a measurement artefact, not a property of the keyword leg. The FTS plan for a query with more than four content tokens is an OR-join over the RAW tokens, and the raw token list keeps stopwords (FtsQueryNormalizer.BuildPlan: 'var orTerms = rawTokens.Count <= MaxOrTerms ? rawTokens.Select(Term).ToList() : ...'), so the OR-join contains 'a' and 'an'. A note that contains the letter-word 'a' therefore matches the query on the keyword leg alone. Measured on 2.0.0: a control note ('There is a bell in the tower and it rings at noon every day of the year without fail.') that shares NO content word with the query is returned by the keyword-only query with 'legs: [{legName: fts, rank: 1}]'. Measured on 1.63.0 with the same content and the same query: the OR-list matches 1 row and the token 'a' alone matches it - identical behaviour, so this is not a 2.0.0 regression. The FtsQueryNormalizer is byte-identical between d06746fc and origin/main. The prior run's 0 must have been read before the note's FTS row existed: measured here, the FTS row is present IMMEDIATELY after the write, so a 0 means the note was not there yet, not that the keyword leg was empty.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: 2.0.0: 'query (keyword only, vectorWeight 0) -> results: [(notes/control.md, 1)]' with 'legs: [{legName: fts, rank: 1}]' for a control that shares no content word with the query. The A/B against 1.63.0: '-- 1.63.0: the OR-list matches 1 row(s); the token a alone matches 1; rows/chunk_index [(1, '0')]' and '-- 2.0.0: the OR-list matches 1 row(s); the token a alone matches 1; rows/chunk_index [(1, '0')]'. The normalizer is unchanged: 'git diff d06746fc origin/main -- src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sqlite/Memory/FtsQueryNormalizer.cs' -> empty.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The hybrid search works, but the keyword leg is far weaker than the prior run's evidence claimed: for any query longer than four content words, the OR-join carries stopwords, so the FTS leg matches most English notes and the vector leg's contribution is masked in the fusion. Any measurement that used 'the FTS leg finds nothing' as a control was measuring the wrong thing. The fix belongs in the OR-join (use the stopword-free token set, as the long-query branch already does), and it is a retrieval-quality change rather than a release blocker for 2.0.0 - but the 1.63.0 report's claim that this query 'cannot be carried by keyword match' should not be carried forward.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, against the 1.63.0 report's item 'memory-search-hybrid-retrieval' (the premise itself)

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, against the rename itself (the surface change 2.0.0 makes)
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The rename's own plan treats it as a hard rename with no alias layer: 'A hard rename breaks every existing client; an alias layer is new work' (docs/work/2026-10-21-tool-surface-rename-and-entry-types.md). The checklist confirms the server side is exact - 30 new names, 30 refusals - so what is left is the client side.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: A client that was CONNECTED across the upgrade keeps its cached tool list, and it is now a list of 30 dead names. This session is the demonstration: the server was upgraded to 2.0.0 during the run, and the agent harness still advertises the 30 pre-rename names. Calling one of them now returns 'Unknown tool: memory_search' (JSON-RPC -32602), and the new names are not callable at all from the same session - 'tools.mcp__ai_raccoon__query does not exist'. The client is not broken; it is holding a stale catalogue. The same shape bites the agent instructions: the framework's refreshed hook matcher targets 'query', so the memory-first gate no longer fires on a 'memory_search' call, and the gate's own message tells the agent to search memory with a tool it can no longer call. The refusal is also a raw JSON-RPC error with no guidance in it: a client that calls a renamed name learns only that the tool is unknown, not that it was renamed.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: In this session, after the live server moved to 2.0.0: 'mcp__ai_raccoon__memory_search' -> 'Error: Request failed (remote): Unknown tool: memory_search'. The harness's catalogue still lists the 30 old names ('count=30', mcp__ai_raccoon__memory_search, ... mcp__ai_raccoon__project_id_token_get) and no new one. A raw call at the live server: 'calling the OLD name on the live server: {"_rpc_error": {"code": -32602, "message": "Unknown tool: memory_search"}}' against 'calling the NEW name on the live server: {"data": {"results": [...]}}' - so the server is right and the client's catalogue is stale. The gate's message during the same window: 'Memory-first: search memory for ... first, then re-run this search.' - an instruction to use a name the server no longer serves.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Three things belong in 2.0.0's release notes and one belongs in a follow-up: (1) a client must reconnect after the upgrade - the tool list is fetched at connect time, so an open session silently keeps a catalogue of dead names; (2) an agent's cached instructions can name tools that no longer exist, and the framework's hook matcher was updated to the new name, so the gate goes dormant until the client refreshes; (3) the unknown-tool error carries no rename hint, which is what the 2.0.1 'unknown tool call guidance' branch is for - this run's evidence supports that work; and (4) the 1.63.0 -> 2.0.0 upgrade is a hard break for every existing client, which the rename plan accepted deliberately.
